_comment: xLSTM retune campaign, REVISED after the 240k extension of the gru/lstm/transformer incumbents (v0.38-v0.47) was evaluated. Run with: uv run python scripts/train_campaign.py --sweep sweep_arch.json [--dry-run]. Each run auto-versions into checkpoints/v<version>/ and is gauntleted (tournament block) against baselines + resnet/temporal incumbents, so it slots into the same Elo ladder. defaults set history=1 (temporal archs ignore stacked history) and pin the temporal + xlstm knobs; each run overrides network.arch=xlstm plus the knobs it varies. Revision rationale (why this differs from the earlier 80k-screen design): the earlier sweep transferred lr=1e-4 as the base because it won ~+97 Elo at 80k on both gru and transformer. The 240k extension overturned that. At lr=1e-4 the transformer PEAKED at 80k (811) then DECAYED to 765; at lr=5e-5 it kept climbing (717->752, still rising at 240k). And recurrent nets learn late: the LSTM did not click until ~90k (445->626 in one 10k window) and rose to 685 by 237k. Since xLSTM is an LSTM descendant (mLSTM+sLSTM): (a) we screen at 240k, not 80k -- an 80k cutoff would misjudge xLSTM the way it would have misjudged the LSTM, and the ladder incumbents are now at 240k so 80k is not comparable; (b) lr=5e-5 is the base for every run, with 1e-4 demoted to ONE probe that tests whether xLSTM decays like the transformer over the long horizon or not; (c) eta=0.5 is the default (the only eta=0.2 recurrent run, the gru, was the weakest of the four), kept as default with one eta=0.2 symmetry probe. The xLSTM-specific axis is the mLSTM/sLSTM composition (network.xlstm_slstm_at): since transformer (~ mLSTM parallel matrix-memory) beat gru (~ sLSTM gated recurrence), we sweep all-mLSTM (fastest on the vanilla sLSTM backend) vs mixed vs all-sLSTM.

runs._comment: Base: canonical lr=5e-5 (the horizon-preferred lr -- it kept climbing to 240k while 1e-4 decayed), default 2-block [mLSTM, sLSTM] stack. The reference every other run builds on.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-base

runs._comment: lr probe: 1e-4 won ~+97 Elo at 80k on gru AND transformer, but over 240k the transformer at 1e-4 peaked at 80k then decayed (811->765). This single run tests whether xLSTM follows that long-horizon decay or is the exception. Demoted from base to probe by the 240k findings.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-lr1e4

runs._comment: All-mLSTM (slstm_at=[] -> 2 mLSTM blocks): the most transformer-like, fully parallel matrix-memory variant, and the fastest on the vanilla sLSTM backend. Tests whether mLSTM's transformer-like memory drives xLSTM here. At the 5e-5 base lr.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-mlstm

runs._comment: All-sLSTM (slstm_at=[0,1] -> 2 sLSTM blocks): the recurrent, gated-memory extreme. Opposite pole from -mlstm; brackets the composition axis. At the 5e-5 base lr.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-slstm

runs._comment: Deeper native stack: 4 blocks, paper-style alternation [mLSTM, sLSTM, mLSTM, sLSTM]. Depth was arch-dependent for the other nets (helped gru, hurt transformer); xLSTM is a native deep-block arch, so one probe. At the 5e-5 base lr.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-4L

runs._comment: Regularization symmetry probe: eta=0.2 vs the canonical 0.5, at the 5e-5 base lr. Expected weak -- the only eta=0.2 recurrent run (gru) was the weakest of the four -- but ablates the choice cleanly.
runs.name: arch-xlstm-eta0.2
